items.title: 独立开发者 Yetone 主导开发的 Alma，在最新一轮 AI Agent 横评中，同时拿下任务通过率和成功成本第三名，把 Claude Code、OpenCode 等知名工具甩在了身后。
items.summary:
独立开发者 Yetone 主导开发的 Alma，在最新一轮 AI Agent 横评中，同时拿下任务通过率和成功成本第三名，把 Claude Code、OpenCode 等知名工具甩在了身后。

这次评测由 AI Agent 基础设施公司 Runta 发起。在当前的榜单快照中，Alma 的任务通过率为 72.7%，仅次于 Codex CLI 的 77.9% 和 Pi 的 72.8%。Claude Code 则为 70.0%。

Alma 不仅通过率更高，完成任务也更省钱。它每成功完成一道题平均花费约 0.80 美元，Claude Code 为 0.94 美元，成本低约 16%。

这次 FrontierHarness v1.1 专门研究一个问题：同样的大模型，换一套 Agent 执行框架，表现究竟能差多少？

评测覆盖 21 组 Harness 配置、5 款大模型和 62 项任务，每项重复 4 次，计划运行 26,040 次，规模达到上一版的 72 倍。所有工具都在统一的云端环境中运行，比较任务成功率、Token 成本和执行速度。

Alma 是一款主打本地运行、长期记忆的 AI Agent，能直接读取和修改代码、执行终端命令、搜索网页，还支持 Skills 和 MCP。它可以自由切换底层模型，不依赖某一家模型厂商。

最近，Alma 还整合了 Herdr。Claude Code、Codex、Pi 等编程 Agent 可以继续在 Herdr 中运行，Alma 则把它们集中到一个聊天界面，查看执行过程、回复问题和批准操作。用户甚至可以通过 iPhone 远程管理电脑上的多个 Agent。

目前评测尚未结束，排名仍会变化。参测模型也仅限 GLM、DeepSeek、Kimi、Muse 等开源模型，没有覆盖 GPT 和 Claude 系列闭源模型。

items.title: Claude要干倒微软了？
items.summary:
Claude要干倒微软了？
11月10日，Anthropic在旧金山发布Claude Whiteboards、Sheets（均为beta）和Meetings，Dashboards转正并更名Claude Data。

同一天，Anthropic更新IPO文件，拟以每股70至78美元发行8.25亿股，估值约1.3万亿至1.4万亿美元，最早下周挂牌。

时间点耐人寻味。上市前夜亮出办公全家桶，等于告诉华尔街：
Claude不只是程序员的工具，还要进入每个白领的日常工作，想象空间从开发者扩大到整个Office。
5月的私募估值已达9650亿美元，首次超过OpenAI。

杀伤力不在单点功能，而在上下文贯通：会议、白板、表格、看板，Claude一路记得来龙去脉，不用在软件之间复制粘贴。
同时它还以Claude for Excel、Word、PowerPoint插件嵌进微软地盘，两条腿走路。

微软当天股价下跌2.2%，年内累计跌幅约20%。
投资者担心的并不是Claude明天就取代Excel，而是按席位收费的办公软件，定价权正在向AI智能体转移。

但微软也不是吃素的。3月推出Copilot Cowork，底层接入Claude；9月Copilot大改版，加入自然语言写代码工具，以及拥有独立身份、全天候待命的Autopilot智能体，配套Agent 365做权限治理，正是大企业最在意的一环。
Copilot还同时接入GPT-6 Astra与Claude Fable 5.1，谁强用谁，两头下注。

所以这不是一边倒的屠杀。微软握着存量、渠道和合规；
Anthropic握着增量、估值和故事，但Sheets仍在beta，复杂需求还得导出xlsx。
Office的护城河在变薄，却远没被填平。

真正的战场只有一个：谁成为员工每天打开的第一个入口。

items.title: The AI Race is Putting Patients at Risk - Progressive.org
items.summary: Indeed, the most frightening risks involving AI are already moving from theory to capability. Frontier models let non-experts code new applications quickly, and soon it may be possible to use AI to create biological agents that can be weaponized. The White House’s own AI Action Plan warns that AI could create new pathways for bad actors to synthesize dangerous pathogens and calls for stronger screening and national security assessment of AI tools and systems. Anthropic has already said its [...] The protection of public health requires similar guidance and oversight. AI can strengthen biosurveillance by finding signals across disparate data, model and predict outbreaks, and help allocate scarce resources. We must build governance into our health system’s infrastructure that includes testing standards and protocols, continuous monitoring, ethics oversight, user education, and clear lines of accountability. [...] Japan created an AI Strategy Headquarters headed by the prime minister and adopted a national AI basic plan. The United Kingdom and Australia are linking their AI safety institutes in order to better evaluate frontier AI model risks. These systems differ, but they have one thing in common - national AI governance.

items.title: Gilbert + Tobin rethinks the business of law with AI
items.summary:
Leaders have to use the technology themselves: experiment, push the boundaries and learn what works. When people see that AI matters to you, it sets the tone and encourages others to engage with it.

We did not mandate usage targets. Instead, we made the technology relevant. Our business transformation team demonstrated workflows tailored to different functions, while videos, showcases, challenges and an early AI bounty surfaced ideas from across the firm. [...] The real value we’ve seen from AI so far hasn’t been about reducing cost or needing fewer people, but freeing our people to focus on the more human side of their work, meeting with clients, coaching their teams and mentoring the future leaders of our industry.

> _“It’s been about…freeing them up to then do the more human side of their work.”_

—Sam Nickless, Partner and Chief Executive Officer, Gilbert + Tobin [...] My team is now able to use it to get “my feedback”, effectively, via ChatGPT. It lets them test their thinking against my context and working style before coming to me. It does not make decisions or speak for me; it helps our conversations start from a stronger place.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s Apology May Be the Only Correct Use of AI - The Atlantic
items.summary: People (me) are always saying about AI, “This is a solution looking for a problem!” and “Who would possibly want to delegate things like knowing information about your childrenor creating works of art to a third-party series of zeroes and ones?” But there are some things in life that nobody wants to do, such as get a root canal, amputate a limb, or deal with your cable provider. Or, perhaps, apologize simultaneously to your employees and your wife of 40 years for jeopardizing your business and [...] Look, I just want to say that if NVIDIA CEO and reported spy-plot target Jensen Huang did get help from AI to write an apology email to his family and company about his affair (he’s said he uses AI to help write all of his first drafts), this might be the one use of AI that makes sense to me.

“Part of embracing this technology is recognizing that we can’t send graduates into the world without knowing how to use these tools,” said Jennifer Totonchy, Ph.D., associate dean of research and graduate programs. “Ensuring our students are comfortable with AI is part of how we prepare them for future careers and stay true to our mission.” 

WHEN AI FALLS SHORT [...] Totonchy sees the skepticism around AI in higher education as an opportunity.  

“Generative AI quickly gained a negative reputation because it was seen as a tool for cheating,” she said. “That misses the point. These tools can work alongside humans, handling routine tasks so people can focus on analysis and decision-making. The sooner institutions move past resistance, the sooner AI can support that work.” 

STUDENTS PUT AI TO WORK [...] “We are also already seeing AI positively impact the quality of patient care in our pharmaceutical rotations, so having AI integrated into our curriculum is eye opening,” Wu said. “I don’t know many other schools that offer this kind of opportunity.”

items.title: The AI Race is Putting Patients at Risk - Progressive.org
items.summary: Indeed, the most frightening risks involving AI are already moving from theory to capability. Frontier models let non-experts code new applications quickly, and soon it may be possible to use AI to create biological agents that can be weaponized. The White House’s own AI Action Plan warns that AI could create new pathways for bad actors to synthesize dangerous pathogens and calls for stronger screening and national security assessment of AI tools and systems. Anthropic has already said its [...] The protection of public health requires similar guidance and oversight. AI can strengthen biosurveillance by finding signals across disparate data, model and predict outbreaks, and help allocate scarce resources. We must build governance into our health system’s infrastructure that includes testing standards and protocols, continuous monitoring, ethics oversight, user education, and clear lines of accountability. [...] Japan created an AI Strategy Headquarters headed by the prime minister and adopted a national AI basic plan. The United Kingdom and Australia are linking their AI safety institutes in order to better evaluate frontier AI model risks. These systems differ, but they have one thing in common - national AI governance.

items.title: Gilbert + Tobin rethinks the business of law with AI

Leaders have to use the technology themselves: experiment, push the boundaries and learn what works. When people see that AI matters to you, it sets the tone and encourages others to engage with it.

We did not mandate usage targets. Instead, we made the technology relevant. Our business transformation team demonstrated workflows tailored to different functions, while videos, showcases, challenges and an early AI bounty surfaced ideas from across the firm. [...] The real value we’ve seen from AI so far hasn’t been about reducing cost or needing fewer people, but freeing our people to focus on the more human side of their work, meeting with clients, coaching their teams and mentoring the future leaders of our industry.

> _“It’s been about…freeing them up to then do the more human side of their work.”_

—Sam Nickless, Partner and Chief Executive Officer, Gilbert + Tobin [...] My team is now able to use it to get “my feedback”, effectively, via ChatGPT. items.title: Jensen Huang’s Apology May Be the Only Correct Use of AI - The Atlantic
items.summary: People (me) are always saying about AI, “This is a solution looking for a problem!” and “Who would possibly want to delegate things like knowing information about your childrenor creating works of art to a third-party series of zeroes and ones?” But there are some things in life that nobody wants to do, such as get a root canal, amputate a limb, or deal with your cable provider. Or, perhaps, apologize simultaneously to your employees and your wife of 40 years for jeopardizing your business and [...] Look, I just want to say that if NVIDIA CEO and reported spy-plot target Jensen Huang did get help from AI to write an apology email to his family and company about his affair (he’s said he uses AI to help write all of his first drafts), this might be the one use of AI that makes sense to me.

WHEN AI FALLS SHORT [...] Totonchy sees the skepticism around AI in higher education as an opportunity.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: Exclusive: OpenAI targets Microsoft's GitHub with deal
items.summary:
OpenAI will acquire Pierre Computer, a developer tools startup whose technology is already embedded in Codex, the company told Axios exclusively.

Why it matters:OpenAI is joining a slew of companies challenging Microsoft's GitHub as AI agents take on more coding work. The platform has acted as a central repository and nerve center for software development for many years.

Zoom out:GitHub has faced a number of reliability issues and outages as AI coding has taken off. [...] Financial terms were not disclosed. Pierre's open-source projects will remain open-source.

Between the lines:Earlier this week, OpenAI revealed Pando, built to handle the explosion of code generated by AI agents.

   OpenAI says Pando reduced the time needed to push code changes by nearly 80%. 
   The company is now exploring ways to make the technology available to customers. [...] Cursor, now owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX, launched GitHub rival Origin in August.
   Former GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke, who launched a new coding startup, announced a competing product last month.
   Microsoft owns nearly a quarter of OpenAI, although the two companies also compete in a variety of ways, a dynamic that is common across the competitive AI landscape.

Driving the news: OpenAI plans to integrate Pierre's Code Storage function into Codex, where Pierre's technology is already used.
